\section*{Question 5}

Consider the differential equation \(\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{y-1}{x^{2}}\), where \(x \neq 0\).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] On the axes provided, sketch a slope field for the given differential equation at the nine points indicated.
(Note: Use the axes provided in the exam booklet.)
\item[(b)] Find the particular solution \(y=f(x)\) to the differential equation with the initial condition \(f(2)=0\).
\item[(c)] For the particular solution \(y=f(x)\) described in part (b), find \(\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} f(x)\).
\item[(a)]
![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/9d72369d-8f1d-482d-b417-6aff56485376-1.jpg?height=408&width=548&top_left_y=1001&top_left_x=451)
\item[(b)] \(\frac{1}{y-1} d y=\frac{1}{x^{2}} d x\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
& \ln |y-1|=-\frac{1}{x}+C \\
& |y-1|=e^{-\frac{1}{x}+C} \\
& |y-1|=e^{C} e^{-\frac{1}{x}} \\
& y-1=k e^{-\frac{1}{x}}, \text { where } k= \pm e^{C} \\
& -1=k e^{-\frac{1}{2}} \\
& k=-e^{\frac{1}{2}} \\
& f(x)=1-e^{\left(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{x}\right)}, x>0
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[(c)] \(\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} 1-e^{\left(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{x}\right)}=1-\sqrt{e}\)
\end{itemize}
